1: Gorgeous Carat by You Higuri (Blu) is a lush historical boys' love story with a jewel-thief mystery at its heart. In Belle Époque Paris, the young Ray Courland is sold by his mother to Florian, Count de la Roche, a wealthy and charming nobleman. Ray soon learns that his new master is secretly Noir, a notorious thief of precious gems. It's a good pick for readers who love period costumes, elegant art, and slow-burning tension.
4: Anne Freaks by Yua Kotegawa (ADV) is a dark psychological thriller about two teenagers with terrible secrets. After Yuri Shimizu kills his abusive mother, a strange girl named Anne Mitsuya appears and helps him bury the body. In return, she wants his help with her own plan for revenge against the father who leads a dangerous cult. It's tense, unsettling, and fast-moving, best for readers who like crime stories with an edge.
5: Antique Bakery by Fumi Yoshinaga (DMP) is a warm, witty josei comedy-drama set in a small pastry shop. Keiichiro Tachibana opens a late-night bakery and hires Yusuke Ono, a brilliant pastry chef with a complicated past, along with an ex-boxer apprentice and a loyal childhood friend. Between cakes and customers, old history slowly comes to the surface. It's a great fit for readers who enjoy found-family stories, sharp dialogue, and lovingly drawn desserts.
8: Guardian Angel Getten by Minene Sakurano (Raijin) is a lighthearted comedy-romance with a dash of Chinese mythology. Middle schooler Tasuke Shichiri receives a mysterious ring from his traveling father. When he looks through it, out pops Shaolin, a guardian spirit sworn to protect him from all harm, whether he needs it or not. It's a sweet, silly read for fans of classic magical-girlfriend stories.
9: Gun Blaze West by Nobuhiro Watsuki (Viz Media) is a Wild West action-adventure from the creator of Rurouni Kenshin. In 1870s America, young Viu Bannes dreams of reaching Gun Blaze West, a legendary place where only the strongest gunfighters can go. A wandering drifter named Marcus Homer teaches him to shoot and sets him on the road. It's a short, spirited read for fans of classic shonen adventure and cowboy stories.
11: Gundam Seed Destiny by Masatsugu Iwase (Del Rey) is a mecha war drama set in the Cosmic Era of Gundam Seed. Two years after the last war, an uneasy peace holds between Naturals and Coordinators. Shinn Asuka, a young ZAFT pilot who lost his family in the earlier fighting, takes the controls of the new Impulse Gundam just as conflict breaks out again. It's a good fit for Gundam fans who want the story in a compact form.
12: Hanako and the Terror of Allegory by Sakae Esuno (Tokyopop) is a creepy supernatural mystery from the creator of Future Diary. Daisuke Aso is a detective who specializes in allegories, urban legends that come to life and haunt the people who believe in them. With help from his strange assistant Hanako, he takes on cases no ordinary investigator could handle. It's a great pick for readers who enjoy spooky case-of-the-week stories.
14: Nadesico by Kia Asamiya (CPM) is a sci-fi comedy based on the anime Martian Successor Nadesico. Akito Tenkawa just wants to be a cook, but he ends up aboard the Nadesico, a privately built battleship with a quirky crew, fighting mysterious invaders from Jupiter. Asamiya gives the story his own spin on the characters and events. It's a fun read for fans of mecha anime who like plenty of humor with their space battles.
17: Neon Genesis Evangelion: Angelic Days by Fumino Hayashi (ADV) is a romantic comedy that reimagines Evangelion as an everyday school story. Here, Shinji Ikari is an ordinary student with a bossy childhood friend named Asuka, and a quiet new transfer student named Rei shakes up his routine. Familiar faces appear in new roles, with lighter stakes and more heart. It's a fun alternate take for Evangelion fans who want to see the characters happy.
19: The Earl and the Fairy by Ayuko, based on the novels by Mizue Tani (Viz Media), is a romantic fantasy set in Victorian Britain. Lydia Carlton is a fairy doctor, someone who can see and talk to fairies, though few people believe in them anymore. Her life changes when the charming Edgar Ashenbert, who claims to be the heir of the Blue Knight Earl, hires her to help find a legendary sword. It's a lovely pick for fans of historical romance with magic.
20: Attack on Titan: Lost Girls by Hiroshi Seko and Ryosuke Fuji (Kodansha) is a side story that takes a closer look at two of the series' toughest young women. It follows Annie Leonhart and Mikasa Ackerman through stories set alongside the main series, filling in what they think, feel, and keep hidden. The tone stays dark and tense, with more room for quiet character moments. It's best for readers who already know Attack on Titan and want more.
21: Avalon High: Coronation by Meg Cabot (Tokyopop) is a manga continuation of her novel Avalon High, blending teen romance with Arthurian legend. Ellie Harrison has learned that her boyfriend Will might be the reincarnation of King Arthur, and that their friends may be playing old roles too. Now forces from the legend are stirring again, and the danger is real. It's a light, readable pick for fans of Meg Cabot and modern takes on Camelot.
22: The Golden Sheep by Kaori Ozaki (Vertical) is a quiet, emotional drama about friendship and growing up. Tsugu moves back to her hometown and is thrilled to reunite with her childhood friends. But the friends she remembers have changed, and each of them is carrying something they don't want to talk about. It's a thoughtful, sometimes painful read for anyone who likes realistic stories about teenagers and the bonds that hold them together.
23: The Haunted Bookstore by Shinobumaru (Seven Seas) is a cozy supernatural story about books, spirits, and family. Kaori is a human girl raised by Shinonome, a book-loving yokai who runs a secondhand bookstore for the spirits of a parallel world. As she helps match customers with the right stories, she starts to wonder about her own past. It's a warm, gentle read for fans of slow-paced fantasy and bookish heroines.
25: Nightschool: The Weirn Books by Svetlana Chmakova (Yen Press) is a supernatural mystery set in a school that opens only after dark. Alex is a young weirn, a kind of witch, who has been homeschooled while her older sister Sarah works as the Nightschool's keeper. Then Sarah disappears, and everyone else seems to have forgotten she ever existed. It's a smart, atmospheric read for fans of magic-school stories with a mystery to solve.
26: Ninja High School by Ben Dunn (Antarctic Press) is a zany action comedy and one of the longest-running American manga-style comics. Ordinary teenager Jeremy Feeple suddenly finds himself the target of two determined suitors: Ichi, a young ninja, and Asrial, an alien princess. Their rivalry drags him into chaos involving ninja clans, space armies, and plenty of slapstick. It's a fun, goofy read for fans of classic anime parodies and over-the-top school comedy.
41: I Am a Hero by Kengo Hanazawa (Dark Horse) is a grim seinen horror story about a very ordinary man in an extraordinary crisis. Hideo Suzuki is a 35-year-old manga assistant whose career is stalled and whose imagination tends to run away with him. When a strange sickness starts turning people into violent monsters, he finds himself surviving with only his wits and a hunting shotgun. It's best for mature readers who like slow-building, realistic zombie horror.
42: Otherside Picnic by Iori Miyazawa (J-Novel Club) is an eerie sci-fi horror light novel series about two young women exploring another world. College student Sorawo has been sneaking into the Otherside, a strange place full of creatures from internet ghost stories, when she meets Toriko, who is searching there for a missing friend. They team up to explore its dangers and collect its valuable artifacts. It's a great pick for fans of creepypasta and slow-burn yuri.
43: Our Dreams at Dusk by Yuhki Kamatani (Seven Seas) is a gentle, heartfelt drama about finding a place to belong. High schooler Tasuku Kaname is terrified after rumors spread that he is gay. On the worst day of his life, he follows a mysterious woman to a drop-in center where people of all kinds of identities gather. It's a moving, thoughtful read for anyone who enjoys quiet stories about community and self-acceptance.
45: Bleach by Tite Kubo (Viz Media) is a supernatural action series about a teenager caught between the living and the dead. Ichigo Kurosaki has always been able to see ghosts. When a Soul Reaper named Rukia Kuchiki is wounded protecting his family from a monstrous Hollow, she passes her powers to him, and Ichigo takes over her job of guarding souls. It's a stylish, fast-paced read for fans of sword fights and big ensemble casts.
46: The Scum Villain's Self-Saving System by Mo Xiang Tong Xiu (Seven Seas) is a funny, dramatic fantasy light novel with a boys' love storyline. Shen Yuan dies while ranting about a terrible web novel and wakes up inside it as Shen Qingqiu, the cruel teacher doomed to be destroyed by his disciple Luo Binghe. To survive, he decides to be kind to the boy instead. It's a great pick for fans of xianxia, comedy, and slow-burn romance.
47: Papillon by Miwa Ueda (Del Rey) is a shojo drama about self-confidence and sibling rivalry. Ageha is the quiet, plain twin, while her sister Hana is cute, popular, and good at everything. When the boy Ageha has loved since childhood falls for Hana instead, she decides it's time to change. With help from an unusual school counselor, she starts to find her own wings. It's a good read for fans of school romance and makeover stories.
52: Boys Run the Riot by Keito Gaku (Kodansha) is a heartfelt drama about identity, friendship, and fashion. Ryo is a high schooler who is a transgender boy, though few people know it, and he feels most like himself in streetwear. When he meets Jin, a new transfer student who shares his love of clothes, the two decide to start their own fashion brand. It's an honest, encouraging read for anyone who likes stories about finding your people.
55: Initial D by Shuichi Shigeno (Kodansha) is a street-racing drama that became a classic of car culture. Takumi Fujiwara is a quiet high schooler who has spent years delivering tofu for his father's shop, driving the family's old Toyota AE86 down a winding mountain road before dawn. Without realizing it, he has become an incredibly skilled driver, and local racers are starting to notice. It's a great pick for car fans and anyone who loves sports rivalries.
63: To Love Ru by Saki Hasemi and Kentaro Yabuki (Seven Seas) is a romantic comedy with a sci-fi twist and plenty of fanservice. Shy high schooler Rito Yuki can never quite confess to his crush, Haruna. Then Lala, a cheerful runaway princess from another planet, crash-lands into his life and decides he's going to be her fiancé. It's silly, energetic fun for older teen readers who enjoy harem comedies.
65: Tokyo Mew Mew a la Mode by Reiko Yoshida and Mia Ikumi (Tokyopop) is a magical girl sequel to Tokyo Mew Mew. With Ichigo away in England, a cheerful new girl named Berry Shirayuki gains animal powers and joins the Mew Mew team. Together they protect Tokyo from a new threat while Berry juggles school, friendship, and a crush. It's a sweet, bright read for magical girl fans and anyone who loved the original series.
66: Pokémon Journeys by Machito Gomi (Viz Media) is a kid-friendly adventure based on the Pokémon Journeys anime. Ash Ketchum and Pikachu team up with Goh, a boy who wants to catch every Pokémon there is, and the two become research fellows at a Pokémon lab. Their work sends them traveling across every region in the Pokémon world. It's a fun, easy read for young fans and anyone who grew up with Ash and Pikachu.
70: Psycho-Pass by Hikaru Miyoshi (Viz Media) is a sci-fi crime thriller based on the anime of the same name. In a future Japan, the Sibyl System scans citizens' minds and measures their likelihood of committing a crime. Rookie inspector Akane Tsunemori joins a police unit that hunts these latent criminals with the help of enforcers, who are latent criminals themselves. It's a sharp, thought-provoking read for fans of dystopian detective stories.
71: Pumpkin Scissors by Ryotaro Iwanaga (Del Rey) is a military action drama about the hard work of rebuilding after a war. Lieutenant Alice Malvin, a determined young noblewoman, leads Pumpkin Scissors, an army unit devoted to war relief. Her team gains a quiet, towering new member named Randel Oland, a former soldier with a mysterious lantern and a dangerous past. It's a good fit for readers who like action with serious themes.
75: R.O.D: Read or Die by Hideyuki Kurata (Viz Media) is a lively action-adventure about a woman who loves books more than anything. Yomiko Readman is a shy, bookish substitute teacher who is also an agent for the British Library, with the power to bend paper into shields, blades, and wings. When rare books and important people start disappearing, she's called into action. It's a fun pick for book lovers who also enjoy spy stories.
77: Ral Grad by Tsuneo Takano and Takeshi Obata (Viz Media) is a fantasy action adventure from the artist of Death Note. Ral has been raised his whole life in darkness, and for good reason: inside his body lives Grad, a powerful shadow beast. When Ral finally steps into the light, the two set off together to fight the demons that threaten the world. It's a short, energetic read for fans of classic shonen fantasy.
78: Ratman by Sekihiko Inui (Tokyopop) is an action comedy that turns the superhero story upside down. Shuto Katsuragi is a short but big-hearted kid who dreams of becoming a hero. Instead, he's tricked into becoming Ratman, an agent for Jackal, a secret organization of villains. Shuto still tries to do good in his new role. It's a fun read for superhero fans who enjoy a lovable underdog and lots of humor.
85: Danganronpa: The Animation by Takashi Tsukimi (Dark Horse) is a mystery thriller adapted from the anime based on the hit video game. Makoto Naegi is an ordinary student chosen as the Ultimate Lucky Student at the elite Hope's Peak Academy. Soon after arriving, he and his classmates find themselves trapped inside the school by Monokuma, a bear who forces them into a deadly game. It's a gripping read for fans of whodunits and dark puzzles.
86: Darling in the Franxx by Kentaro Yabuki (Seven Seas) is a sci-fi romance based on the mecha anime. In a ruined future, children are trained to pilot giant machines called Franxx in pairs to fight monsters. Hiro, a boy who has failed as a pilot, meets Zero Two, a mysterious girl with horns who chooses him as her partner. It's a good pick for fans of the anime and of mecha stories with a romantic core.
88: Restaurant to Another World by Junpei Inuzuka (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy about good food and the people who come to eat it. Western Restaurant Nekoya is an ordinary diner in Tokyo, except that every Saturday its door opens into a world of elves, dragons, and adventurers. The chef serves them dishes they have never tasted before, and each customer has a story. It's a relaxing, mouth-watering read for fans of gentle fantasy and food manga.
90: Villainess Level 99 by Satori Tanabata (One Peace Books) is a fantasy comedy about a heroine who is a little too good at leveling up. Yumiella Dolkness realizes she has been reborn as the hidden final boss of an otome game. She doesn't plan to be evil, but she does train hard, and soon she's at level 99 while everyone else is far behind. It's a fun pick for fans of villainess stories and overpowered heroines.
95: Lady Snowblood by Kazuo Koike and Kazuo Kamimura (Dark Horse) is a seinen revenge drama set in Meiji-era Japan. Yuki was born in prison to a mother who had sworn vengeance against the people who destroyed her family. Raised and trained to carry out that revenge, Yuki grows up into a deadly assassin who hides her blade inside an umbrella. It's a striking, mature read for fans of samurai stories and Koike's work on Lone Wolf and Cub.
100: Wish by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a gentle fantasy romance about an angel and the man who saved her. Doctor Shuichiro Kudo rescues a tiny angel named Kohaku from a pair of crows. Grateful, she offers to grant him a wish, but he says he has none, so Kohaku decides to stay with him until he does. It's a sweet, quiet story, perfect for CLAMP fans and readers who like soft, fairy-tale romance.
101: Legal Drug by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a supernatural mystery with a touch of boys' love. Kazahaya Kudo and Rikuo Himura work at the Green Drugstore, but their boss Kakei also gives them unusual side jobs. Each task calls on their hidden psychic powers and pulls them into strange cases. It's a stylish, atmospheric read for CLAMP fans, especially anyone who enjoyed xxxHolic.
108: X by CLAMP (Viz Media) is a dark supernatural action drama about the end of the world. Kamui Shiro returns to Tokyo after six years away, carrying powerful psychic abilities and a promise to his late mother. Two groups, the Dragons of Heaven and the Dragons of Earth, are waiting for him, because his choice will decide whether humanity survives. It's a moody, dramatic read for longtime CLAMP fans and lovers of apocalyptic fantasy.
112: Dramacon by Svetlana Chmakova (Tokyopop) is a romantic drama set in the world of anime conventions. Christie is an aspiring writer at her first convention, helping sell the comic she created with her boyfriend. Things get complicated when she meets Matt, a moody cosplayer who wears sunglasses indoors. It's a charming, funny read for anyone who has ever been to a con, and a great pick for fans of realistic romance.
115: Zodiac P.I. by Natsumi Ando (Tokyopop) is a mystery comedy about a girl detective with a cosmic edge. Lili Hoshizawa seems like an ordinary middle schooler, but she secretly solves crimes using astrology and a magical star-shaped item. As she cracks cases around her town, she also deals with friendship and crushes. It's a light, fun read for younger shojo fans who enjoy puzzles and magical girls.
116: Zombiepowder by Tite Kubo (Viz Media) is an action adventure from the creator of Bleach. Gamma Akutabi is a mysterious swordsman searching for the Rings of the Dead, legendary jewels said to produce Zombiepowder, a substance that can bring the dead back to life. Along the way he picks up a young thief named Elwood and a fiery journalist named Wolfina. It's a short, stylish read for Bleach fans and anyone who loves Western-style action.
118: Earthian by Yun Kouga (Blu) is a sci-fi fantasy with a boys' love storyline. Angels from the planet Eden are sent to Earth to judge whether humanity deserves to survive. Chihaya, an angel who loves humans, and Kagetsuya, a proud angel who distrusts them, are partnered for the mission, and their bond grows as they record the good and bad of human life. It's a dreamy, emotional read for fans of classic shojo and BL.
119: 86 -Eighty-Six- by Asato Asato (Yen Press) is a sci-fi war drama about the soldiers a nation pretends don't exist. The Republic of San Magnolia claims its war against the drones of the Legion is fought by unmanned machines. In truth, the pilots are the 86, people of minority descent stripped of their rights. Young commander Vladilena Milizé is assigned to lead a squad of them led by Shinei Nouzen. It's a powerful pick for fans of military sci-fi.
121: Elfen Lied by Lynn Okamoto (Dark Horse) is a violent seinen horror story with a tragic heart. Lucy is a Diclonius, a girl with horns and invisible arms that can tear through anything, who escapes from a secret research facility. College student Kouta and his cousin Yuka find her on a beach, injured and acting like a gentle child named Nyu. It's an intense read for mature readers who can handle heavy gore and dark themes.
129: Whispered Words by Takashi Ikeda (One Peace Books) is a sweet, funny yuri romance set in high school. Sumika is tall, athletic, and serious, and she has secretly loved her best friend Ushio for years. Ushio, meanwhile, falls for one cute girl after another without ever noticing how Sumika feels. Their circle of quirky friends adds plenty of comedy. It's a lovely pick for readers who enjoy slow-burn romance and slice-of-life school stories.
131: Manga Dogs by Ema Toyama (Kodansha) is a comedy about life as a teenage manga artist. Kanna Tezuka is fifteen and already a published pro, so she enrolls in her high school's new manga course hoping for peace and quiet. Instead she's adopted by three clueless, handsome classmates who all want her to teach them how to make manga. It's a quick, goofy read for anyone curious about the manga industry or fond of school comedies.
133: Kingdom Hearts: Chain of Memories by Shiro Amano (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure based on the video game. After the events of the first Kingdom Hearts, Sora, Donald, and Goofy arrive at Castle Oblivion, a strange place where each floor brings back memories of past journeys. But the deeper they go, the more Sora forgets. It's a light, fun read for younger readers and fans of the games who enjoy Disney worlds and Final Fantasy cameos.
137: I'm the Villainess, So I'm Taming the Final Boss by Sarasa Nagase (Yen Press) is a romantic fantasy comedy with a bold heroine. When her fiancé, the crown prince, breaks off their engagement, Aileen suddenly remembers her past life and realizes she's the villainess of an otome game. To avoid her doomed ending, she sets out to win over the game's final boss, the demon king Claude. It's a fun pick for fans of clever heroines and villainess stories.
138: Trigun by Yasuhiro Nightow (Dark Horse) is a sci-fi Western about the most wanted man on a desert planet. Vash the Stampede has a sixty-billion-double-dollar bounty on his head and a reputation for leaving destruction everywhere he goes. But the man himself turns out to be a goofy, donut-loving pacifist who will do almost anything to avoid killing. It's a great pick for fans of action, humor, and gunslinger stories with heart.
145: R.O.D: Read or Dream by Hideyuki Kurata (Viz Media) is an action adventure spin-off of Read or Die. In Hong Kong, three sisters named Michelle, Maggie, and Anita run the Paper Sisters Detective Agency. Like Yomiko Readman, they can control paper, and they use their powers to take on strange cases involving books and the people who love them. It's a fun read for fans of the R.O.D. series and lighthearted action.
146: I'm in Love with the Villainess by Inori (Seven Seas) is a yuri romantic comedy light novel. An overworked office worker wakes up as Rae Taylor, the commoner heroine of her favorite otome game. Instead of chasing the game's princes, she sets her sights on the one character she has always adored: Claire François, the haughty noble villainess. It's a funny, heartfelt pick for fans of villainess stories who want the romance to go a different way.
150: Black Bullet by Shiden Kanzaki and Morinohon (Yen Press) is a sci-fi action story about survival in a world overrun by monsters. Humanity lives behind walls that keep out the Gastrea, a virus that turns living things into monsters. Rentaro Satomi works as a Civil Officer, protecting the city alongside Enju, one of the Cursed Children who carry the virus and gain superhuman abilities. It's a fast, dark read for fans of post-apocalyptic battle stories.
153: The Irregular at Magic High School by Tsutomu Sato (Yen Press) is a sci-fi light novel series about magic treated as a modern science. Siblings Tatsuya and Miyuki Shiba enroll at an elite academy for magicians. Miyuki is a star student, while Tatsuya is ranked near the bottom, but he is hiding far more ability than anyone realizes. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy detailed magic systems, school drama, and an unbeatable lead.
156: Romantic Killer by Wataru Momose (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy that pokes fun at romance. High schooler Anzu Hoshino is happiest with her video games, her chocolate, and her cat. Then a pushy wizard named Riri takes all three away and starts throwing classic love-story setups at her, determined to make her fall for someone. Anzu is just as determined to resist. It's a laugh-out-loud read for anyone who loves to tease shojo clichés.
158: Yukarism by Chika Shiomi (Viz Media) is a shojo fantasy romance about past lives. Yukari Kobayakawa is a seventeen-year-old who writes popular historical novels set in Japan's Edo period. His books are so accurate because he remembers his past life as Yumurasaki, a famous courtesan. When he meets people from that life again, old loves and old dangers return. It's a lovely pick for readers who enjoy reincarnation stories and historical settings.
161: Sweet Blue Flowers by Takako Shimura (Viz Media) is a gentle, realistic yuri drama about first love. Fumi Manjome and Akira Okudaira were close as little girls, then drifted apart when Fumi's family moved away. Years later, they meet again as high schoolers at different girls' schools, and their friendship picks up where it left off. It's a quiet, thoughtful read for fans of coming-of-age stories and slow, honest romance.
162: Corrector Yui by Keiko Okamoto (Tokyopop) is a magical girl adventure set inside a computer network. Yui Kasuga is a cheerful girl who isn't good with computers, until she's pulled into ComNet, a vast online world. There she becomes a Corrector, working with friendly programs to fight a virus that threatens to take over the network. It's a fun read for younger readers and fans of retro tech and magical girl series.
163: Aldnoah.Zero by Olympus Knights and Pinakes (Yen Press) is a mecha war drama based on the anime. Long ago, ancient technology found on Mars gave rise to the Vers Empire. Now Earth and Mars are at war again, and Inaho Kaizuka, a calm and clever high schooler, is pulled into the fighting with only a training robot and his wits. It's a good pick for fans of mecha anime and tactical battles.
164: Twisted-Wonderland: The Book of Heartslabyul by Yana Toboso (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure based on the Disney mobile game. A student is pulled into a strange world and lands at Night Raven College, an elite magic school whose dorms are inspired by Disney villains. Stuck there with no magic, they get tangled up with the strict, rule-bound Heartslabyul dorm. It's a fun pick for fans of the game, Disney, and magic school stories.
170: A Bride's Story by Kaoru Mori (Yen Press) is a gorgeously drawn historical drama set in nineteenth-century Central Asia. Amir, a skilled rider and hunter, is married off at twenty to Karluk, a boy eight years younger, and comes to live with his family in a town along the Silk Road. As she settles in, the story explores daily life, family, and tradition. It's a rich, rewarding read for fans of history and detailed art.
178: Doomsday with My Dog by Yu Ishihara (Yen Press) is a quiet, bittersweet slice of life about the end of the world. Humanity is all but gone, but one girl keeps walking through the empty landscape with Haru, her loyal shiba inu. The story follows their small days together, often seen through Haru's simple, funny dog's-eye view. It's a gentle, touching read for dog lovers and anyone who enjoys calm post-apocalyptic stories.
179: Howl's Moving Castle by Hayao Miyazaki (Viz Media) is a film comic that tells the Studio Ghibli movie using frames from the film itself. Sophie is a shy young hatmaker until a jealous witch curses her into an old woman. Looking for a way to break the spell, she finds work as a housekeeper in the walking castle of Howl, a vain and mysterious wizard. It's a lovely way to revisit the film, perfect for Ghibli fans of all ages.
185: Spirited Away by Hayao Miyazaki (Viz Media) is a film comic that retells the Studio Ghibli movie using frames from the film itself. Ten-year-old Chihiro is moving to a new town when her family stumbles into a spirit world. After her parents are turned into pigs, she must work in a bathhouse for spirits to save them. It's a beautiful way to revisit the film, and a great pick for Ghibli fans of any age.
188: xxxHolic Rei by CLAMP (Kodansha) is a supernatural mystery that returns to the world of xxxHolic. Kimihiro Watanuki is a high schooler plagued by spirits who stumbles into a shop run by Yuko Ichihara, a witch who grants wishes for a price. To pay off his wish, Watanuki goes to work for her, and strange customers keep arriving. It's an atmospheric read for CLAMP fans and anyone who loves spooky, stylish stories.
194: The Electric Tale of Pikachu by Toshihiro Ono (Viz Media) is a lighthearted adventure inspired by the early Pokémon anime. Ash Ketchum sets out to become a Pokémon master, but his first partner, Pikachu, has a mind of its own. Along the way they meet new friends, battle rivals, and run into plenty of trouble. It's a fun, nostalgic read for longtime Pokémon fans and a great pick for kids.
196: Assassin's Creed: Blade of Shao Jun by Minoji Kurata (Viz Media) is a historical action story set in the world of the Assassin's Creed games. In 1526, Shao Jun, one of the last surviving members of the Chinese Brotherhood of Assassins, returns to Ming-dynasty China. She has come to hunt down the Eight Tigers, a group of powerful Templars. It's a fast, stylish read for fans of the games and martial arts action.
